meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 11: JSON-RPC 2.0 Fundamentals (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about MCP's JSON-RPC envelope are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Request ids must be unique among the sender's outstanding requests
A response's id must match the id of the request it answers
A response contains either result or error, never both
params may be either an array or an object, as in base JSON-RPC
Responses must arrive in the order the requests were sent

questions.explanation: Result and error are mutually exclusive, ids correlate the pair, and MCP additionally forbids reusing an id that is still outstanding. Ordering is never guaranteed, and MCP's params is an object carrying the reserved _meta key.

questions.question: Which pairings of condition and standard JSON-RPC error code are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Arguments do not match the declared schema — -32602
The client is missing a required capability — -32603
Method name is not recognised by the server — -32601
Body is not valid JSON at all — -32700
The request is valid but the backend API timed out — -32600

questions.explanation: -32700 parse error, -32601 method not found and -32602 invalid params are the standard codes for those conditions. -32600 means the envelope itself is not a valid request, and a missing capability is the MCP-specific -32021, not the internal-error code.

questions.question: Which statements about MCP's use of the JSON-RPC server-error range are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Application-specific codes should be allocated outside -32768 to -32000
-32000 to -32019 is legacy: new implementations should not allocate codes there
-32020 to -32099 is reserved for codes defined by the MCP specification
Receivers may assume -32001 means the request headers disagreed with the body
Every code in the reserved range now maps to a fixed HTTP status code

questions.explanation: The allocation policy splits the range as in A and B and pushes new application codes outside the reserved block. -32001 was a draft number for HeaderMismatch before renumbering to -32020; in the final spec it carries no meaning, and receivers MUST NOT assume one.
